hero.title: Friday
hero.lead: You land at 08:10. The rest is up to you :)

paras: Friday's free, so you get to pick. Tap whatever looks good and I'll do the Planung (planning). We'll do a few things and take our time :)

steps.title: What do you want to see?
steps.hint: Pick as many as you like.

tiles.label: Old Rome
tiles.sub: The Pantheon, the Trevi Fountain, a house under a church

tiles.label: Rome from above
tiles.sub: Sunset from the Vittoriano roof, Castel Sant'Angelo, the Pincio

tiles.label: The weird stuff
tiles.sub: A bone crypt, a fake dome, a trick corridor

tiles.label: Art that's worth it
tiles.sub: Bernini's marble, three Caravaggios, Haring, Kandinsky

tiles.label: Street food

tiles.label: A proper lunch

arrival.title: You land
arrival.body: We leave your bag at my hostel by Termini and start from there, around 10.

bags.title: Bags to the flat
bags.body: We grab the bags from my hostel and take a taxi to the flat in Pigneto. You'll have been up since before sunrise, so a nap is allowed :)

dinner.title: Dinner
dinner.body: Pizza at Li Rioni, behind the Colosseum.

options.title: Pantheon
options.line: A 1,900-year-old dome with an open hole at the top. Stand in the middle and look up.

options.title: San Clemente
options.line: Two staircases down under a church: a Roman house, a temple of a secret cult, and water running somewhere below.

options.title: Trevi Fountain
options.line: Before 11:30 we see it from the street; after, the steps down to the basin take a €2 ticket.

options.title: Under Trevi's streets
options.line: Stairs down from an old cinema to a Roman house, where the water that feeds the Trevi still runs past.

options.title: Caesar's cats
options.line: The ruins where Caesar was stabbed are home to a cat sanctuary now. They sleep on the old stones.

options.title: Vittoriano roof
options.line: A lift up to the roof of the big white monument at sunset. All of Rome around you, the old Forums right below.

options.title: Castel Sant'Angelo
options.line: An emperor's tomb turned fortress. A long ramp and some stairs take you up to the terrace, St Peter's dead ahead.

options.title: The Pincio terrace
options.line: We cut through Villa Borghese to a free terrace over Piazza del Popolo, look across at St Peter's dome, then walk down Via Margutta.

rainPlan.text: If it rains, we do the bone crypt instead.

options.title: Bone crypt
options.line: Six small rooms decorated with the bones of about 3,700 people, most of them friars.

options.title: The fake dome
options.line: The church never got its dome, so a painter faked one on the flat ceiling. From the right spot on the floor it looks real.

options.title: The trick corridor
options.line: A colonnade that looks 35 metres deep is under nine. The warrior at the end is about knee high.

options.title: The 17:30 machine
options.line: At 17:30 a 17th-century machine slides a huge painting down like a curtain, with music, and a silver statue appears behind it.

options.title: Statues in a power plant
options.line: Roman marble gods stand between giant black engines in an old power station.

options.title: Pyramid and Keats
options.line: A quiet garden cemetery behind a real Roman pyramid. Keats is buried here.

options.title: Bernini at the Borghese
options.line: Marble that looks soft: Daphne's fingers turning into leaves, David biting his lip mid-throw.

options.title: Three Caravaggios
options.line: Walk in off a street near the Pantheon and three Caravaggios hang in a side chapel.

options.title: The Doria Pamphilj palace
options.line: A family still lives upstairs, and you walk through their gilded Hall of Mirrors to Velázquez's red-faced pope, with Bernini's bust of the same man beside it.

options.title: Keith Haring
options.line: A new show of his in a palace off Piazza Navona: the chalk subway drawings, a motorbike he painted in Rome, and paintings under blacklight.

options.title: Kandinsky
options.line: About seventy of his paintings, most on loan from the Pompidou in Paris, in a palace on Piazza Venezia.

options.title: Maritozzo
options.line: A soft bun split open and packed with cream, at Regoli near Termini, a pastry shop going since 1916.

options.title: Boccione
options.line: A tiny bakery in the Ghetto with no sign. Get the burnt-top fruit cake and the sour cherry tart.

options.title: Biscuit bakery
options.line: An old Trastevere bakery with a 16-metre oven. The trays come straight out to the counter.

options.title: Testaccio market
options.line: A neighbourhood market full of food stalls. The beef sandwich drips, so most people eat it standing up.

options.title: Supplì
options.line: Fried rice balls with mozzarella inside. Break one open and the cheese stretches like a phone cord.

options.title: Trapizzino
options.line: A triangle of crusty pizza bread stuffed with a Roman stew, like chicken cacciatora or meatballs in tomato sauce.

options.title: Lunch at Fortunata
options.line: Women roll and cut pasta by hand in the front window, and that's the pasta you eat.

options.title: Lunch in a hill of pots
options.line: A trattoria dug into a hill made of broken Roman jars. Some walls show the old jars behind glass.

options.title: Pasta class
options.line: Roll and cut fettuccine by hand with a chef, make a tiramisu, then sit down and eat what you made. In English.

options.title: Trastevere
options.line: Small ivy-covered streets across the river, two vintage shops on Via di San Francesco a Ripa, and no plan: we turn wherever looks better.

options.title: The old centre
options.line: Piazza Navona to Campo de' Fiori through the small streets in between, past the Pantheon.

options.title: Aventine keyhole
options.line: Look through a keyhole and St Peter's dome is framed in it. Next door, a terrace of orange trees over the river.

rainPlan.text: If it rains, we see the statues in the power plant instead.

options.title: Aqueduct park
options.line: Roman aqueduct arches nearly 28 metres tall, standing in a field where locals run and walk their dogs.

rainPlan.text: If it rains, we do San Clemente instead.

options.title: Coppedè
options.line: A few streets most people never see. An iron chandelier hangs in a stone arch, and the fountain is all frogs.

options.title: Monti
options.line: The neighbourhood between my hostel and the Colosseum: vintage shops like Pifebo and Humana, a fountain square, and a tiny mosaic chapel if we catch it open.

options.title: The Jewish Ghetto
options.line: A flat loop past a Roman colonnade with a church built into it, a palace sitting on a Roman theatre, and four bronze boys pushing turtles into a fountain. Friday is also 16 October, the day in 1943 the Nazis rounded up over a thousand of Rome's Jews, starting right here, so there may be a commemoration.

options.title: Chariot race in VR
options.line: On the real Circus Maximus track, a headset rebuilds the stands and a chariot race goes past you.

rainPlan.text: If it rains, we do San Clemente instead.

options.title: Noon cannon
options.line: A cannon fires below the Gianicolo terrace at noon. Loud, and the view of Rome is free.

options.title: The nuns' bell
options.line: We ring the convent bell, and if the nuns are around they let us into a chapel painted in the 1240s like a comic strip.

options.title: A lap of the Circus Maximus
options.line: One easy shakeout lap of the old chariot track, about 1.5 km, with the Palatine ruins above you.

options.title: Vespa sidecar
options.line: A driver takes us through the old streets in a vintage Vespa sidecar. One of us rides in the sidecar, one behind the driver, and we swap at the stops.
